d: Snobby Cynthia Holmes schemes with her obnoxious cousin, Skippy, to make the Fonz look foolish at a country club soirée.
Richie, Ralph, and Potsie endure the harassment of "hell week" to prove themselves worthy to enter their college fraternity, Phi Kappa Nu.

Sophomore Joanie Cunningham gets basic back-seat defense tips from Richie and Fonzie before her first "car date" with a senior boy, and then cramps her older brother's style when she and her date show up at his college "make-out" party.
What begins as a humorous escapade with a motorcycle turns into a tragic vigil for the Cunninghams and their friends.

Fonzie's latest romantic interest, a ballet teacher, is secretly yearning to turn professional and dance with the greats in New York. Fonzie, however, has trouble accepting that she may forgo their relationship to pursue her dreams of fame.

When Ralph Malph is hypnotized to cure his fright after a tornado warning is posted, Ralph's loss of fear causes him to tempt fate by suggesting that the Fonz needs training wheels for his stupid motorcycle
Joanie believes she has to smoke to fit in with the cool girls. She ignores the pleas from her family to stop, until the Fonz defines what cool really means
In a poignant, change-of-pace episode titled Fonzie's Blindness, Al barges through the kitchen door at the drive-in and hits Fonzie in the head with a tray of food.
Squiggy forgets his lines in a play written by Shirley, so Laverne and Shirley cover all the parts while a famed Broadway producer watches from the audience.
Lenny and Squiggy’s attempt to start a talent agency lands Laverne and Shirley on national television with Latvian acrobats.
Laverne and Shirley double date with two younger men and wind up at a wild college fraternity party.
The girls search for a precious earring that Laverne lost while she was on a date with a phony Hollywood producer.
Laverne falls for actor, Charles Grodin, and mistakenly interprets his kindness as a romantic gesture.

st: Love Is In The Tar Pits
d: When Lenny falls for an attractive woman, Squiggy becomes fiercely jealous of their friendship.
Laverne and Shirley learn a hysterical lesson about themselves when they flirt with phoniness at a wild party to impress two hot dates.
Laverne takes an unexpected swim when the man she has been dating tries to get out of hot water with his wife.

st: Whatever Happened to the Class of '56?
d: The girls return to Milwaukee for a high school reunion to discover that everyone believes that they are movie stars.
The girls decide to go on a ski weekend and encounter two guys and peril on a ski lift.
Mork gets a pet caterpillar; Exidor begins preaching about reincarnation.
After ruining Fred and Mindy's night, Mork decides he wants to go back to Ork, so Orson shows him what the McConnells' lives would have been like if Mork had never arrived on Earth.
Mork becomes so hopelessly addicted to advertisements that they invade his dreams.
Mork decides to become a priest.
Mork foolishly picks a fight with Mindy in order to "kiss and make up."
Mork and Mindy compete to earn a job working for Nelson.
As Mindy prepares a formal party for Nelson, Mork discovers he's become allergic to Mindy.
Mork instills human emotions in a robot.
Grandma Nussbaum teaches Fonzie and Chachi a lesson in growing old gracefully when they try to convince the feisty granny to move into a retirement home.

Howard's teen-aged niece, K.C., comes to stay with the Cunninghams after a scandal closes her Houston boarding school while Fonzie hopes a night at the circus will help him win little Heather's heart when nothing else seems to work.
After tricking Fonzie into going to a single's camp to help him get over losing steady girlfriend Ashley, Potsie, Chachi and Roger get suckered into a sauna by three con-girls.

st: You Get What You Pay For
d: Howard decides the house needs a second bathroom. Fonzie offers a way to have it installed and save Howard money as well.
Joanie encounters trouble when she accepts a student teaching job at Patton High.
His friends are baffled when Fonzie refuses to speak in his own defense after he is accused of manhandling a student and brought before the school board's disciplinary court.
Joanie tries to help an angry fifteen year old girl kick a drug habit that threatens to get her kicked out of school.
